description: Use this when a user asks what a medical service or hospital stay costs, or what was actually paid for it, for example an office visit, an MRI, a colonoscopy, physical therapy, a knee replacement or a pneumonia stay, in England (care home weekly costs paid by councils) (country GB), Norway (state tariff fees for doctors, psychologists, dentists, physiotherapists) (country NO), Sweden (dental care reference prices) (country SE), Singapore (hospital bills for medical conditions) (country SG), the United States (Medicare fees for medical equipment) (country US) or the United States (what Medicare paid doctors and hospitals) (country US). Returns the official average amount the public health insurer allowed per service (doctors' services, in an office or a facility) or paid per hospital stay (by hospital-stay group), nationally or for one state where the source publishes it, with the number of services or discharges behind it, the share the insurer itself paid, the national average for comparison and the data year, plus the official source and licence. These are public-insurance rates (price_type official_statistic): what the insurer allowed or paid, NOT private-insurance negotiated prices or cash prices, which are usually higher, and not a quote. A published average, so the range fields are null. Facility figures are the doctor's fee only; the hospital's or surgery centre's fee is separate. How fresh: England (care home weekly costs paid by councils): annual: one edition each autumn (2024-25 published 23 Oct 2025, tables revised 13 Nov 2025); Norway (state tariff fees for doctors, psychologists, dentists, physiotherapists): helsedirektoratet publishes new tariff files about twice a year; we read the page and use the newest file for each field; Sweden (dental care reference prices): TLV publishes a new tariff file once or twice a year; we read the page and use the file in force today; Singapore (hospital bills for medical conditions): annual benchmark file (data year 2023, file last updated 15 May 2026); every answer states its data year; the United States (Medicare fees for medical equipment): quarterly (January, April, July, October); the release is stated in every answer; the United States (what Medicare paid doctors and hospitals): annual: one calendar year at a time (the 2024 data year was released in 2026); every answer states its data year. Do not use for a quote or what a specific hospital or doctor charges, private-insurance or out-of-pocket costs, drug or prescription prices, dental or vision plans, or other countries.

basis.description: US only: dmepos = Medicare's fee schedule for medical equipment and supplies (wheelchairs, CPAP, oxygen, walkers, test strips). Leave out for doctor and hospital prices.

country.description: GB = England only for care homes (average weekly cost councils pay for nursing and residential care, GBP; official statistic, not what private self-funders pay); NO = Norway (state tariff fees for doctors, psychologists, dentists and physiotherapists under…

service.description: The medical service: plain words ('office visit', 'MRI lower back', 'knee replacement'), a billing code or a hospital-stay group code, as the country notes list them. Required. GB: care home costs only: 'care home', 'nursing care' or…

setting.description: office = a doctor's office (whole service); facility = hospital outpatient or surgery centre (doctor's fee only); inpatient = a hospital stay. Leave out to use the usual setting for the service. GB: not used, leave out. NO: not used…

state.description: A state or territory, where the source publishes one (the country notes say how to write it). Leave out for the national average. GB: leave out for the England average, or give an English region ('North East', 'London', 'South West'...)…
